newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - December 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - December 17.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Tuesday's edition of Daily Variety:
NEW YORK - In one of the larger publishing deals of the year, senior presidential adviser George Stephanopoulos landed an advance of $2.75 million from Little, Brown & Co. for his memoirs.

HOLLYWOOD - With the weekend entry of Sony's box office champ, "Jerry Maguire," to the holiday marketplace, four of Hollywood's highest paid actors are now vying for theatergoers' attention -- and entertainment dollars.

HOLLYWOOD - In the wake of Time Warner placing a monetary value on E! Entertainment Television on Dec. 9, the MSO partners who own stakes in the network have until early February to determine if they want to buy out Time Warner's 58 percent interest in E! or sell their shares to the corporation.

NEW YORK - After turning the unlikely subject of porn king Larry Flynt into an acclaimed film, director Milos Forman and screenwriters Scott Alexander and Larry Karaszewski are zeroing in on an equally offbeat figure: Andy Kaufman.
HOLLYWOOD - News Corp 's Fox Broadcasting Co is looking to develop a TV show based on the Scott Adams comic strip Dilbert, which has caught fire during the past year.

WASHINGTON - President Bill Clinton apparently knows more about the proposed TV ratings system than he led reporters to believe last week. He told reporters Friday that he had not yet had a report on an industry proposal to rate its own programming. What he did not say is that Vice President Al Gore and Motion Picture Assn of America head Jack Valenti had discussed the issue in detail a day earlier.
